target.title: fix: authorize exact commands inside Gateway wrappers
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Gateway `system.run` sends Windows commands as `cmd.exe /d /s /c <command>`, so the host rejected the unmatched outer wrapper before evaluating an exact allow rule for the requested command.
- Why it matters: an operator could approve `hostname`, yet the same command still failed through the real Gateway-to-node path.
- What changed: parse shell wrappers before approval; only an unmatched default deny may defer to nested targets, and each nested target must match an exact allow rule. Explicit outer/inner denies and prompt behavior still win.
- User impact: exact approved commands work through Gateway-wrapped Windows execution without granting a broad shell rule.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no new command capability, default permission, network call, credential path, or release artifact.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs / instructions
- [x] Tests / validation
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Tray / WinUI UX
- [x] Windows node capability
- [ ] Local MCP / `winnode`
- [x] Gateway / connection / pairing
- [ ] Setup / onboarding
- [x] Permissions / privacy / security
- [x] Tests / CI / docs

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #971
- Related openclaw/openclaw#104735
- [x] Related to a bug or regression

## Validation

- `./build.ps1` — passed; Shared, CLI, WinNode CLI, SetupEngine, and WinUI built.
- `dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore` — 2,736 passed, 31 skipped, 0 failed.
- `dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore` — 1,669 passed, 0 failed.
- Focused gateway-wrapper regression set — 4 passed, 0 failed.
- Three fresh autoreview passes; the first found a broad-inner-rule bypass, the repair requires exact nested rules, and the final review reported no actionable findings.
- `./scripts/validate-mxc-e2e.ps1` — blocked before the scenario: the isolated unpackaged ARM64 WinUI test host crashed during startup in `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll` (`0xc000027b`, `80070057`) on two fresh runs, before MCP or `system.run` was reached. The production-signed Hub and real Gateway pairing work on the same Surface; this environmental harness blocker is outside the changed shared approval code.

## Real behavior proof

- Environment tested: Surface ARM64, Windows 11 `10.0.26200`; OpenClaw Hub `0.6.12`; OpenClaw Gateway on `clawmac`.
- PR head / commit tested: `2f172d1e4e5b54075a4d2bc37d84a81ad86869fd` (patch-identical remote Surface validation checkout).
- Exact steps or command run: paired the Hub to the live Gateway, installed an exact `hostname` allow rule, then asked the Gateway agent to execute `hostname` with `exec host=node`.
- Evidence after fix: focused tests exercise the exact Gateway argv `cmd.exe /d /s /c hostname`, explicit outer deny, explicit inner deny, and piped-command rejection.
- Observed result: before the fix, the live Surface returned `denied by exec policy` despite the exact inner allow rule. The current-head tests now authorize only the exact inner command while retaining fail-closed wrapper parsing and deny precedence.
- Screenshot/artifact links verified? N/A
- Not verified / blocked: live current-head node invocation awaits a runnable ARM64 debug host; the mandatory E2E script is blocked by the startup crash documented above.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? Yes
- Data access scope changed? No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: wrapped commands can now use inner allow rules. The mitigation is intentionally strict: only unmatched default-deny wrappers defer, every parsed target must match an exact allow rule, wrapper parse errors fail closed, prompt decisions still apply to the full wrapper, and explicit outer or inner denies still win.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.
